1.name: Brock
1.info:
Theory: Brock utilizes a Rock/Ground defense core with Sturdy triggers. Eviolite Rhyhorn provides extreme physical bulk, while Huge Power Life Orb Marill poses a massive offensive Water/Fairy threat. Geodude holds a Choice Band to deal massive surprise damage or use Self-Destruct.

How to Counter: Special Grass-type or Water-type moves will shred his Rock-types, but beware of Rhyhorn's Poison Jab. Carry a Ghost-type or a Pokémon with Protect to safely absorb Geodude's Self-Destruct. Break Sturdy leads with multi-hit moves or entry hazards.

2.name: Misty
2.info:
Theory: Misty runs a highly synergized Rain weather core. Politoed sets rain automatically via Drizzle, which activates Psyduck's Swift Swim to double its Speed and sweep with Life Orb boosted Water attacks. Mega Gyarados acts as a heavy physical breaker, while Chinchou covers their Electric weakness with Volt Absorb.

How to Counter: The best counter is overriding the weather. Use a Sand Stream or Drought user to clear the rain. Bulky Grass and Dragon types can pivot into Hydro Pumps. Target Politoed immediately to prevent rain setup, and avoid Electric moves when Chinchou is healthy.

3.name: Lt. Surge
3.info:
Theory: Surge is a highly offensive pivot specialist centered around Electric Terrain. Raichu holds Electrium Z to unleash massive Gigavolt Havoc, and Magneton/Electivire exploit Volt Switch to constantly keep momentum and wear down your team.

How to Counter: Ground-types are absolutely mandatory to block Volt Switch and completely shut down his momentum. Lightning Rod or Motor Drive abilities can also absorb Electric moves. Watch out for grass/ice/water coverage moves on his pivots.

4.name: Erika
4.info:
Theory: Erika runs a Sun weather core. Drought sets up sunlight, which activates Chlorophyll on her speed sweepers and enables instant, high-power Solar Beam attacks and boosted Fire-type coverage to melt standard Ice/Steel counters.

How to Counter: Rain or Sand weather setters are incredibly useful here to negate the Sun speed boosts and force Solar Beam into a two-turn charge. Bulky Dragon, Fire, and Poison types are great pivots. Use Safety Goggles or Poison-types to avoid Sleep Powder / Spore.

5.name: Sabrina
5.info:
Theory: Sabrina runs a high-synergy Trick Room team designed to reverse speed tiers. She sets up Trick Room using slow, extremely bulky Psychic pivots, enabling monstrously high-damage, low-speed attackers like Armarouge (Choice Specs) and Hatterene to sweep.

How to Counter: Stall out the Trick Room turns (5 turns) using Protect, Substitute, or defensive Dark and Steel-type pivots. Bring your own slow tanks that can thrive under Trick Room, or use Taunt / Roar to stop her Trick Room setters from setting it up in the first place.

b2.name: Rival 2
b2.info: Rival 2 keeps starter logic: the Fire, Water, or Grass slot becomes the rival starter line based on your starter choice.

baby1.name: Baby Pokemon
baby1.info: Theory: Uses Eviolite on baby Pokémon to create surprisingly bulky threats with good coverage. Suggested Encounters: Strong physical attackers or Knock Off users like Corphish/Dewott to remove Eviolites. How to run: Focus down Wynaut carefully to avoid Counter/Mirror Coat, and use priority or faster Pokémon to handle Magby and Elekid.

superfan1.name: Superfan 1
superfan1.info: Theory: Uses your team-ish when you beat Brock but upgraded a lot (lots of flex here can't pre-make). Expect a well-rounded hyper offense. Suggested Encounters: Bulky waters like Quagsire, or reliable pivots to absorb U-turns and Volt Switches. How to run: Pivot carefully around Primeape and Raichu-Alola. Keep entry hazards up to break their Focus Sashes or punish switching.

adminarcher.name: Admin Archer
adminarcher.info: Archer brings an elite Dark/Poison shell: sleep pressure, trapping, ruin abilities, hazards, and fast poison sweepers. Prepare for status control and very little breathing room.
